question: Latvia is seeking an additional allocation of approximately EUR 7 billion in the next EU budget. This is intended to cover higher defence spending and the economic consequences of severing ties with Russia. The cost of the policy of cutting ties with Russia is thus beginning to be shifted onto the common European budget. 1.
Does the Commission regard Latvia’s request as an admission that the policy towards Russia is already costing Member States so much that they are unable to bear the costs themselves?
Does the Commission actually intend to give Latvia those EUR 7 billion?
Does the Commission consider it sustainable for every further tightening of policy towards Russia to result in a new request for money from Brussels?
